programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E1 Revolution And The Boy King For decades, Western explorers and archaeologists had dominated the search for Egypt's ancient past. But in 1919, a nationwide uprising led by Saad Zaghloul reshaped the country's future. Britain granted Egypt limited independence in 1922, sparking new demands for control over its own heritage. In the midst of this political upheaval, British archaeologist Howard Carter uncovered the tomb of Tutankhamun - an extraordinary find that became a global sensation and transformed Egyptology overnight.

programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E2 The Fight For Egypt's Past Carter returns to Tutankhamun's tomb, where the unveiling of the coffins and the death mask captivates the world. But his return comes with new conditions - Egypt insists that all treasures remain in the country, an important nationalist victory. But foreign archaeologists continue to control most major digs.

programme.title: Lost Treasures of Egypt
programme.desc: S3 E2 Secrets of Egypt's Queens Archaeologists hunt for clues to how the queens of ancient Egypt ruled in a society dominated by men. They enter an unexplored pyramid in search of the burial chamber of a mysterious queen who lived 4500 years ago. They investigate how one of the few women to ever rule as a Pharaoh rose to power, and uncover the surprising role queen Nefertari played in the reign of Ramses the Great.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E1 A Family Matter This episode explores how sitcoms evolve to reflect the changing face of the fundamental social unit that is the family. From I Love Lucy to the blended Brady Bunch, from working class families in All In The Family, Good Times, One Day At A Time, from the groundbreaking Black-ish to Fresh Off The Boat, sitcom humour has helped broaden our horizons and open our minds to what a modern family can be.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E5 Sex & The Sitcom This episode explores the revolution of sex in sitcoms. Since America has long found it easier to laugh about sex than talk seriously about it, sitcom humour has had a critical role ushering in a new era of openness, not just towards sex, but toward women's rights and gender identity.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E3 Just Friends Friends, Seinfeld, Living Single. So many of us know the characters in these shows better than most of our real friends. By the 90s, these 'hanging out with friends' sitcoms became the vital force driving the genre and, in many ways, pop culture. But it's earlier shows like The Odd Couple, Happy Days, Laverne, and Golden Girls that set the stage for peak sitcom, and its iconic follow-ups like Curb Your Enthusiasm, Community, and How I Met Your Mother, that bring that form into the new millennium.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E2 Working for Laughs The workplace is a rich source of comedy as it binds vastly different people together with laughter. From The Mary Tyler Moore Show to Murphy Brown, from WKRP to 30 Rock, from Barney Miller to Brooklyn 99, as America's relationship with their jobs changes - and especially as women break through countless workplace barriers - sitcoms evolve in endlessly humorous ways.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Long Weekends
programme.desc: S2 E1 Lisbon Rick visits Lisbon on the banks of the River Tagus, a city in love with its seafood and possibly the best custard tarts in the world. The culinary effects of Portugal's historic explorations are still seen in its dishes with hints of cinnamon and freshly chopped coriander from the east and tomatoes and chillies from the Americas. Rick is inspired to cook the city favourite snack Salt Cod Fritters, delicious Almond Tart - a favourite dish throughout Portugal. With seafood at the forefront of his mind, he makes sure he arrives just in time for Lisbon's famous St Anthony's Day Parade and Sardine Festival.

programme.title: Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore
programme.desc: At 32, Alice Hyatt (Burstyn) watches her dreams slipping away. Instead of a career as a singer, she has an abusive husband, an ill-mannered 12-year-old son and a life in small-town Oklahoma.

programme.title: The Invisible Fight
programme.desc: A young soldier survives an attack from a group of flying kung fu warriors. Hoping to follow in their footsteps, he travels to a local monastery to begin his martial-arts training.

programme.title: The Ideal Palace
programme.desc: Based on the incredible true story of Joseph Ferdinand Cheval comes the remarkable tale of a simple postman who spent 33 years crafting the magnificent 'Ideal Palace'. Everyday Cheval travels along the river Drome from village to village. Quiet and alone, he enjoys the solitude of his rounds, daydreaming about a world full of wonder he can only imagine through postcards. After his wife Philomena gives birth to their daughter Alice, Cheval decides to build Alice a palace fit for a princess. With only his bare hands, his love for his daughter and the dedication of his wife, he starts carefully collecting stones and begins building the historically classified monument.

programme.title: Discovering Film
programme.desc: S13 E2 Denzel Washington Some of the biggest film stars in history rose to fame during the 'golden age' of Hollywood, in the early and mid-20th century. We profile some of these stars who became household names.

programme.title: The Ipcress File
programme.desc: In London, a counter espionage agent deals with his own bureaucracy while investigating the kidnapping and brainwashing of British scientists.

programme.title: All the President's Men
programme.desc: Academy Award winners Robert Redford and Dustin Hoffman star in this true story as Washington Post reporters Carl Bernstein and Bob Woodward, whose investigation of a seemingly minor hotel room break-in uncovers the greatest political scandal in United States history and leads to the downfall of President Richard Nixon.

programme.title: The Invisible Fight
programme.desc: A young soldier survives an attack from a group of flying kung fu warriors. Hoping to follow in their footsteps, he travels to a local monastery to begin his martial-arts training.

programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E1 Revolution And The Boy King For decades, Western explorers and archaeologists had dominated the search for Egypt's ancient past. But in 1919, a nationwide uprising led by Saad Zaghloul reshaped the country's future. Britain granted Egypt limited independence in 1922, sparking new demands for control over its own heritage. In the midst of this political upheaval, British archaeologist Howard Carter uncovered the tomb of Tutankhamun - an extraordinary find that became a global sensation and transformed Egyptology overnight.

programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E2 The Fight For Egypt's Past Carter returns to Tutankhamun's tomb, where the unveiling of the coffins and the death mask captivates the world. But his return comes with new conditions - Egypt insists that all treasures remain in the country, an important nationalist victory. But foreign archaeologists continue to control most major digs.

programme.title: Lost Treasures of Egypt
programme.desc: S3 E2 Secrets of Egypt's Queens Archaeologists hunt for clues to how the queens of ancient Egypt ruled in a society dominated by men. They enter an unexplored pyramid in search of the burial chamber of a mysterious queen who lived 4500 years ago. They investigate how one of the few women to ever rule as a Pharaoh rose to power, and uncover the surprising role queen Nefertari played in the reign of Ramses the Great.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E1 A Family Matter This episode explores how sitcoms evolve to reflect the changing face of the fundamental social unit that is the family. From I Love Lucy to the blended Brady Bunch, from working class families in All In The Family, Good Times, One Day At A Time, from the groundbreaking Black-ish to Fresh Off The Boat, sitcom humour has helped broaden our horizons and open our minds to what a modern family can be.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E5 Sex & The Sitcom This episode explores the revolution of sex in sitcoms. Since America has long found it easier to laugh about sex than talk seriously about it, sitcom humour has had a critical role ushering in a new era of openness, not just towards sex, but toward women's rights and gender identity.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E3 Just Friends Friends, Seinfeld, Living Single. So many of us know the characters in these shows better than most of our real friends. By the 90s, these 'hanging out with friends' sitcoms became the vital force driving the genre and, in many ways, pop culture. But it's earlier shows like The Odd Couple, Happy Days, Laverne, and Golden Girls that set the stage for peak sitcom, and its iconic follow-ups like Curb Your Enthusiasm, Community, and How I Met Your Mother, that bring that form into the new millennium.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E2 Working for Laughs The workplace is a rich source of comedy as it binds vastly different people together with laughter. From The Mary Tyler Moore Show to Murphy Brown, from WKRP to 30 Rock, from Barney Miller to Brooklyn 99, as America's relationship with their jobs changes - and especially as women break through countless workplace barriers - sitcoms evolve in endlessly humorous ways.

programme.desc: S1 E5 The French Pyrenees This is peasant country where, although the people are not wealthy, they eat like kings. He is knighted into an order of serious bread makers, and makes sausages with a professional.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Long Weekends
programme.desc: S2 E1 Lisbon Rick visits Lisbon on the banks of the River Tagus, a city in love with its seafood and possibly the best custard tarts in the world. The culinary effects of Portugal's historic explorations are still seen in its dishes with hints of cinnamon and freshly chopped coriander from the east and tomatoes and chillies from the Americas. Rick is inspired to cook the city favourite snack Salt Cod Fritters, delicious Almond Tart - a favourite dish throughout Portugal. With seafood at the forefront of his mind, he makes sure he arrives just in time for Lisbon's famous St Anthony's Day Parade and Sardine Festival.

programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E1 Revolution And The Boy King For decades, Western explorers and archaeologists had dominated the search for Egypt's ancient past. But in 1919, a nationwide uprising led by Saad Zaghloul reshaped the country's future. Britain granted Egypt limited independence in 1922, sparking new demands for control over its own heritage. In the midst of this political upheaval, British archaeologist Howard Carter uncovered the tomb of Tutankhamun - an extraordinary find that became a global sensation and transformed Egyptology overnight.

programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E2 The Fight For Egypt's Past Carter returns to Tutankhamun's tomb, where the unveiling of the coffins and the death mask captivates the world. But his return comes with new conditions - Egypt insists that all treasures remain in the country, an important nationalist victory. But foreign archaeologists continue to control most major digs.

programme.title: Leonardo da Vinci
programme.desc: S1 E2 The Disciple of Experience (2) Later, in Milan, Da Vinci joins Duke Sforza's court, begins writing treatises, and paints a monumental fresco depicting the Last Supper.

programme.title: Lost Treasures of Egypt
programme.desc: S3 E2 Secrets of Egypt's Queens Archaeologists hunt for clues to how the queens of ancient Egypt ruled in a society dominated by men. They enter an unexplored pyramid in search of the burial chamber of a mysterious queen who lived 4500 years ago. They investigate how one of the few women to ever rule as a Pharaoh rose to power, and uncover the surprising role queen Nefertari played in the reign of Ramses the Great.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E1 A Family Matter This episode explores how sitcoms evolve to reflect the changing face of the fundamental social unit that is the family. From I Love Lucy to the blended Brady Bunch, from working class families in All In The Family, Good Times, One Day At A Time, from the groundbreaking Black-ish to Fresh Off The Boat, sitcom humour has helped broaden our horizons and open our minds to what a modern family can be.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E5 Sex & The Sitcom This episode explores the revolution of sex in sitcoms. Since America has long found it easier to laugh about sex than talk seriously about it, sitcom humour has had a critical role ushering in a new era of openness, not just towards sex, but toward women's rights and gender identity.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E3 Just Friends Friends, Seinfeld, Living Single. So many of us know the characters in these shows better than most of our real friends. By the 90s, these 'hanging out with friends' sitcoms became the vital force driving the genre and, in many ways, pop culture. But it's earlier shows like The Odd Couple, Happy Days, Laverne, and Golden Girls that set the stage for peak sitcom, and its iconic follow-ups like Curb Your Enthusiasm, Community, and How I Met Your Mother, that bring that form into the new millennium.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E2 Working for Laughs The workplace is a rich source of comedy as it binds vastly different people together with laughter. From The Mary Tyler Moore Show to Murphy Brown, from WKRP to 30 Rock, from Barney Miller to Brooklyn 99, as America's relationship with their jobs changes - and especially as women break through countless workplace barriers - sitcoms evolve in endlessly humorous ways.

programme.desc: S1 E5 The French Pyrenees This is peasant country where, although the people are not wealthy, they eat like kings. He is knighted into an order of serious bread makers, and makes sausages with a professional.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Long Weekends
programme.desc: S2 E1 Lisbon Rick visits Lisbon on the banks of the River Tagus, a city in love with its seafood and possibly the best custard tarts in the world. The culinary effects of Portugal's historic explorations are still seen in its dishes with hints of cinnamon and freshly chopped coriander from the east and tomatoes and chillies from the Americas. Rick is inspired to cook the city favourite snack Salt Cod Fritters, delicious Almond Tart - a favourite dish throughout Portugal. With seafood at the forefront of his mind, he makes sure he arrives just in time for Lisbon's famous St Anthony's Day Parade and Sardine Festival.

programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E1 Revolution And The Boy King For decades, Western explorers and archaeologists had dominated the search for Egypt's ancient past. But in 1919, a nationwide uprising led by Saad Zaghloul reshaped the country's future. Britain granted Egypt limited independence in 1922, sparking new demands for control over its own heritage. In the midst of this political upheaval, British archaeologist Howard Carter uncovered the tomb of Tutankhamun - an extraordinary find that became a global sensation and transformed Egyptology overnight.

programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E2 The Fight For Egypt's Past Carter returns to Tutankhamun's tomb, where the unveiling of the coffins and the death mask captivates the world. But his return comes with new conditions - Egypt insists that all treasures remain in the country, an important nationalist victory. But foreign archaeologists continue to control most major digs.

programme.title: Leonardo da Vinci
programme.desc: S1 E2 The Disciple of Experience (2) Later, in Milan, Da Vinci joins Duke Sforza's court, begins writing treatises, and paints a monumental fresco depicting the Last Supper.

programme.title: Lost Treasures of Egypt
programme.desc: S3 E2 Secrets of Egypt's Queens Archaeologists hunt for clues to how the queens of ancient Egypt ruled in a society dominated by men. They enter an unexplored pyramid in search of the burial chamber of a mysterious queen who lived 4500 years ago. They investigate how one of the few women to ever rule as a Pharaoh rose to power, and uncover the surprising role queen Nefertari played in the reign of Ramses the Great.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E1 A Family Matter This episode explores how sitcoms evolve to reflect the changing face of the fundamental social unit that is the family. From I Love Lucy to the blended Brady Bunch, from working class families in All In The Family, Good Times, One Day At A Time, from the groundbreaking Black-ish to Fresh Off The Boat, sitcom humour has helped broaden our horizons and open our minds to what a modern family can be.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E5 Sex & The Sitcom This episode explores the revolution of sex in sitcoms. Since America has long found it easier to laugh about sex than talk seriously about it, sitcom humour has had a critical role ushering in a new era of openness, not just towards sex, but toward women's rights and gender identity.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E3 Just Friends Friends, Seinfeld, Living Single. So many of us know the characters in these shows better than most of our real friends. By the 90s, these 'hanging out with friends' sitcoms became the vital force driving the genre and, in many ways, pop culture. But it's earlier shows like The Odd Couple, Happy Days, Laverne, and Golden Girls that set the stage for peak sitcom, and its iconic follow-ups like Curb Your Enthusiasm, Community, and How I Met Your Mother, that bring that form into the new millennium.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E2 Working for Laughs The workplace is a rich source of comedy as it binds vastly different people together with laughter. From The Mary Tyler Moore Show to Murphy Brown, from WKRP to 30 Rock, from Barney Miller to Brooklyn 99, as America's relationship with their jobs changes - and especially as women break through countless workplace barriers - sitcoms evolve in endlessly humorous ways.

programme.desc: Step into one of the most famous theatres in the world - the Bolshoi, and get an exclusive glimpse of what happens behind the curtain. Often an instrument of politics, scandals and yet a symbol of the highest artistic achievements and sacrifices.

programme.title: Inside Oxford Street

programme.desc: S1 E5 The French Pyrenees This is peasant country where, although the people are not wealthy, they eat like kings. He is knighted into an order of serious bread makers, and makes sausages with a professional.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Long Weekends
programme.desc: S2 E1 Lisbon Rick visits Lisbon on the banks of the River Tagus, a city in love with its seafood and possibly the best custard tarts in the world. The culinary effects of Portugal's historic explorations are still seen in its dishes with hints of cinnamon and freshly chopped coriander from the east and tomatoes and chillies from the Americas. Rick is inspired to cook the city favourite snack Salt Cod Fritters, delicious Almond Tart - a favourite dish throughout Portugal. With seafood at the forefront of his mind, he makes sure he arrives just in time for Lisbon's famous St Anthony's Day Parade and Sardine Festival.

programme.desc: S11 E4 Freddie There's an emergency arrival at Battersea this week - a beautiful lurcher with a terrible injury in need of urgent surgery. Paul is on hand when he arrives to help calm him down and comfort him.

programme.title: Vintage Voltage
programme.desc: S2 E4 Land Rover Series 2A The Land Rover series 2A from 1970 is a high-profile classic car, a global icon of rough-tough engineering. But its' owner is keen to keep a low profile and wants to bankroll the project from afar, giving Moggy and the team free rein to turn this much-loved offroad, working car into a 21st century four by four with a long future ahead of it.

programme.title: Peter Andre's Greek Odyssey
programme.desc: S1 E3 Vliho Bay Peter Andre jumps ship and sets off on a solo diving adventure whilst Dimitri discovers the cause of the dying palm trees round the Mediterranean. The 'taste off' is replaced by a cook off that threatens to be a washout but, having shopped 'til she dropped, Charlotte is determined it will go ahead.

programme.title: Peter Andre's Greek Odyssey
programme.desc: S1 E4 Spartochori En route to Spartochori the crew circumnavigate Skorpios - a small Island with a big past. Sparochori is a very traditional small Greek village perched high above Porto Spilia. With only one restaurant worthy of the name they pitted the owner against his chef in the Taste-off Challenge. Charlotte and Peter test balance and courage by trying to hoverboard - do they succeed and who will be the best?

programme.title: Berlin: Stories Of The City
programme.desc: S1 E2 The Cold War After Germany's defeat in the Second World War, Berlin was divided at the historic Potsdam conference in 1945 and its division would become a symbol for the Cold War. The division would last almost half a century, symbolised by the construction of the Berlin Wall.

programme.title: SBS World News ᴺᵉʷ
programme.desc: E81 The latest reports and analysis of major national and international news of the day from Australia's only world news service.

programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E1 Revolution And The Boy King For decades, Western explorers and archaeologists had dominated the search for Egypt's ancient past. But in 1919, a nationwide uprising led by Saad Zaghloul reshaped the country's future. Britain granted Egypt limited independence in 1922, sparking new demands for control over its own heritage. In the midst of this political upheaval, British archaeologist Howard Carter uncovered the tomb of Tutankhamun - an extraordinary find that became a global sensation and transformed Egyptology overnight.

programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E2 The Fight For Egypt's Past Carter returns to Tutankhamun's tomb, where the unveiling of the coffins and the death mask captivates the world. But his return comes with new conditions - Egypt insists that all treasures remain in the country, an important nationalist victory. But foreign archaeologists continue to control most major digs.

programme.title: Leonardo da Vinci
programme.desc: S1 E2 The Disciple of Experience (2) Later, in Milan, Da Vinci joins Duke Sforza's court, begins writing treatises, and paints a monumental fresco depicting the Last Supper.

programme.title: Lost Treasures of Egypt
programme.desc: S3 E2 Secrets of Egypt's Queens Archaeologists hunt for clues to how the queens of ancient Egypt ruled in a society dominated by men. They enter an unexplored pyramid in search of the burial chamber of a mysterious queen who lived 4500 years ago. They investigate how one of the few women to ever rule as a Pharaoh rose to power, and uncover the surprising role queen Nefertari played in the reign of Ramses the Great.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E1 A Family Matter This episode explores how sitcoms evolve to reflect the changing face of the fundamental social unit that is the family. From I Love Lucy to the blended Brady Bunch, from working class families in All In The Family, Good Times, One Day At A Time, from the groundbreaking Black-ish to Fresh Off The Boat, sitcom humour has helped broaden our horizons and open our minds to what a modern family can be.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E5 Sex & The Sitcom This episode explores the revolution of sex in sitcoms. Since America has long found it easier to laugh about sex than talk seriously about it, sitcom humour has had a critical role ushering in a new era of openness, not just towards sex, but toward women's rights and gender identity.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E3 Just Friends Friends, Seinfeld, Living Single. So many of us know the characters in these shows better than most of our real friends. By the 90s, these 'hanging out with friends' sitcoms became the vital force driving the genre and, in many ways, pop culture. But it's earlier shows like The Odd Couple, Happy Days, Laverne, and Golden Girls that set the stage for peak sitcom, and its iconic follow-ups like Curb Your Enthusiasm, Community, and How I Met Your Mother, that bring that form into the new millennium.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E2 Working for Laughs The workplace is a rich source of comedy as it binds vastly different people together with laughter. From The Mary Tyler Moore Show to Murphy Brown, from WKRP to 30 Rock, from Barney Miller to Brooklyn 99, as America's relationship with their jobs changes - and especially as women break through countless workplace barriers - sitcoms evolve in endlessly humorous ways.

programme.title: The Sculpture
programme.desc: A philanthropist Basil Sellers and an artist Terrance Plowright come together to create an impressive, multimillion dollar public sculpture symbolic of Australia's Indigenous and migrant heritage. However, in a world where public art is both admired and scorned, both are pushed to the limit as many obstacles threaten to derail their good intentions.

programme.title: Food Sail Love
programme.desc: E1 Chioggia Narelle and Patrick are in the small fishing town of Chioggia, preparing the yacht for its voyage. Located at the southern end of the Venice Lagoon, we'll be shown around this lovely town and be introduced to some of the colourful people they have come to know here over the years. Then they visit the local commercial fish auction to meet up with a buyer who selects produce for one of the town's finest restaurants.

programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E1 Revolution And The Boy King For decades, Western explorers and archaeologists had dominated the search for Egypt's ancient past. But in 1919, a nationwide uprising led by Saad Zaghloul reshaped the country's future. Britain granted Egypt limited independence in 1922, sparking new demands for control over its own heritage. In the midst of this political upheaval, British archaeologist Howard Carter uncovered the tomb of Tutankhamun - an extraordinary find that became a global sensation and transformed Egyptology overnight.

programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E2 The Fight For Egypt's Past Carter returns to Tutankhamun's tomb, where the unveiling of the coffins and the death mask captivates the world. But his return comes with new conditions - Egypt insists that all treasures remain in the country, an important nationalist victory. But foreign archaeologists continue to control most major digs.

programme.title: Lost Treasures of Egypt
programme.desc: S3 E2 Secrets of Egypt's Queens Archaeologists hunt for clues to how the queens of ancient Egypt ruled in a society dominated by men. They enter an unexplored pyramid in search of the burial chamber of a mysterious queen who lived 4500 years ago. They investigate how one of the few women to ever rule as a Pharaoh rose to power, and uncover the surprising role queen Nefertari played in the reign of Ramses the Great.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E1 A Family Matter This episode explores how sitcoms evolve to reflect the changing face of the fundamental social unit that is the family. From I Love Lucy to the blended Brady Bunch, from working class families in All In The Family, Good Times, One Day At A Time, from the groundbreaking Black-ish to Fresh Off The Boat, sitcom humour has helped broaden our horizons and open our minds to what a modern family can be.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E5 Sex & The Sitcom This episode explores the revolution of sex in sitcoms. Since America has long found it easier to laugh about sex than talk seriously about it, sitcom humour has had a critical role ushering in a new era of openness, not just towards sex, but toward women's rights and gender identity.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E3 Just Friends Friends, Seinfeld, Living Single. So many of us know the characters in these shows better than most of our real friends. By the 90s, these 'hanging out with friends' sitcoms became the vital force driving the genre and, in many ways, pop culture. But it's earlier shows like The Odd Couple, Happy Days, Laverne, and Golden Girls that set the stage for peak sitcom, and its iconic follow-ups like Curb Your Enthusiasm, Community, and How I Met Your Mother, that bring that form into the new millennium.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E2 Working for Laughs The workplace is a rich source of comedy as it binds vastly different people together with laughter. From The Mary Tyler Moore Show to Murphy Brown, from WKRP to 30 Rock, from Barney Miller to Brooklyn 99, as America's relationship with their jobs changes - and especially as women break through countless workplace barriers - sitcoms evolve in endlessly humorous ways.

programme.title: The Ideal Palace
programme.desc: Based on the incredible true story of Joseph Ferdinand Cheval comes the remarkable tale of a simple postman who spent 33 years crafting the magnificent 'Ideal Palace'. Everyday Cheval travels along the river Drome from village to village. Quiet and alone, he enjoys the solitude of his rounds, daydreaming about a world full of wonder he can only imagine through postcards. After his wife Philomena gives birth to their daughter Alice, Cheval decides to build Alice a palace fit for a princess. With only his bare hands, his love for his daughter and the dedication of his wife, he starts carefully collecting stones and begins building the historically classified monument.

programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E1 Revolution And The Boy King For decades, Western explorers and archaeologists had dominated the search for Egypt's ancient past. But in 1919, a nationwide uprising led by Saad Zaghloul reshaped the country's future. Britain granted Egypt limited independence in 1922, sparking new demands for control over its own heritage. In the midst of this political upheaval, British archaeologist Howard Carter uncovered the tomb of Tutankhamun - an extraordinary find that became a global sensation and transformed Egyptology overnight.

programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E2 The Fight For Egypt's Past Carter returns to Tutankhamun's tomb, where the unveiling of the coffins and the death mask captivates the world. But his return comes with new conditions - Egypt insists that all treasures remain in the country, an important nationalist victory. But foreign archaeologists continue to control most major digs.

programme.title: Leonardo da Vinci
programme.desc: S1 E2 The Disciple of Experience (2) Later, in Milan, Da Vinci joins Duke Sforza's court, begins writing treatises, and paints a monumental fresco depicting the Last Supper.

programme.title: Lost Treasures of Egypt
programme.desc: S3 E2 Secrets of Egypt's Queens Archaeologists hunt for clues to how the queens of ancient Egypt ruled in a society dominated by men. They enter an unexplored pyramid in search of the burial chamber of a mysterious queen who lived 4500 years ago. They investigate how one of the few women to ever rule as a Pharaoh rose to power, and uncover the surprising role queen Nefertari played in the reign of Ramses the Great.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E1 A Family Matter This episode explores how sitcoms evolve to reflect the changing face of the fundamental social unit that is the family. From I Love Lucy to the blended Brady Bunch, from working class families in All In The Family, Good Times, One Day At A Time, from the groundbreaking Black-ish to Fresh Off The Boat, sitcom humour has helped broaden our horizons and open our minds to what a modern family can be.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E5 Sex & The Sitcom This episode explores the revolution of sex in sitcoms. Since America has long found it easier to laugh about sex than talk seriously about it, sitcom humour has had a critical role ushering in a new era of openness, not just towards sex, but toward women's rights and gender identity.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E3 Just Friends Friends, Seinfeld, Living Single. So many of us know the characters in these shows better than most of our real friends. By the 90s, these 'hanging out with friends' sitcoms became the vital force driving the genre and, in many ways, pop culture. But it's earlier shows like The Odd Couple, Happy Days, Laverne, and Golden Girls that set the stage for peak sitcom, and its iconic follow-ups like Curb Your Enthusiasm, Community, and How I Met Your Mother, that bring that form into the new millennium.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E2 Working for Laughs The workplace is a rich source of comedy as it binds vastly different people together with laughter. From The Mary Tyler Moore Show to Murphy Brown, from WKRP to 30 Rock, from Barney Miller to Brooklyn 99, as America's relationship with their jobs changes - and especially as women break through countless workplace barriers - sitcoms evolve in endlessly humorous ways.

Young Conan is sold off to slave traders where, as he grows in size and strength, his masters train and condition him for the barbaric games in the arena, where the winners walk away with their honour and the losers pay with their lives. Conan soon becomes so powerful that his masters realise that they will not be able to control him for much longer and release him into the wild. There, he lives by his wits as a thief and adventurer, until he inadvertently steals a gemstone from Thulsa Doom. Vowing to avenge his parents, Conan wages war against Doom and his cult of snake worshippers. programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E1 Revolution And The Boy King For decades, Western explorers and archaeologists had dominated the search for Egypt's ancient past. But in 1919, a nationwide uprising led by Saad Zaghloul reshaped the country's future. Britain granted Egypt limited independence in 1922, sparking new demands for control over its own heritage. In the midst of this political upheaval, British archaeologist Howard Carter uncovered the tomb of Tutankhamun - an extraordinary find that became a global sensation and transformed Egyptology overnight.

programme.title: The Race For Ancient Egypt In Colour
programme.desc: S1 E2 The Fight For Egypt's Past Carter returns to Tutankhamun's tomb, where the unveiling of the coffins and the death mask captivates the world. But his return comes with new conditions - Egypt insists that all treasures remain in the country, an important nationalist victory. But foreign archaeologists continue to control most major digs.

programme.title: Lost Treasures of Egypt
programme.desc: S3 E2 Secrets of Egypt's Queens Archaeologists hunt for clues to how the queens of ancient Egypt ruled in a society dominated by men. They enter an unexplored pyramid in search of the burial chamber of a mysterious queen who lived 4500 years ago. They investigate how one of the few women to ever rule as a Pharaoh rose to power, and uncover the surprising role queen Nefertari played in the reign of Ramses the Great.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E1 A Family Matter This episode explores how sitcoms evolve to reflect the changing face of the fundamental social unit that is the family. From I Love Lucy to the blended Brady Bunch, from working class families in All In The Family, Good Times, One Day At A Time, from the groundbreaking Black-ish to Fresh Off The Boat, sitcom humour has helped broaden our horizons and open our minds to what a modern family can be.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E5 Sex & The Sitcom This episode explores the revolution of sex in sitcoms. Since America has long found it easier to laugh about sex than talk seriously about it, sitcom humour has had a critical role ushering in a new era of openness, not just towards sex, but toward women's rights and gender identity.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom
programme.desc: S1 E3 Just Friends Friends, Seinfeld, Living Single. So many of us know the characters in these shows better than most of our real friends. By the 90s, these 'hanging out with friends' sitcoms became the vital force driving the genre and, in many ways, pop culture. But it's earlier shows like The Odd Couple, Happy Days, Laverne, and Golden Girls that set the stage for peak sitcom, and its iconic follow-ups like Curb Your Enthusiasm, Community, and How I Met Your Mother, that bring that form into the new millennium.

programme.title: History of the Sitcom

From The Mary Tyler Moore Show to Murphy Brown, from WKRP to 30 Rock, from Barney Miller to Brooklyn 99, as America's relationship with their jobs changes - and especially as women break through countless workplace barriers - sitcoms evolve in endlessly humorous ways.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Long Weekends
programme.desc: S2 E1 Lisbon Rick visits Lisbon on the banks of the River Tagus, a city in love with its seafood and possibly the best custard tarts in the world. The culinary effects of Portugal's historic explorations are still seen in its dishes with hints of cinnamon and freshly chopped coriander from the east and tomatoes and chillies from the Americas. Rick is inspired to cook the city favourite snack Salt Cod Fritters, delicious Almond Tart - a favourite dish throughout Portugal. With seafood at the forefront of his mind, he makes sure he arrives just in time for Lisbon's famous St Anthony's Day Parade and Sardine Festival.

programme.title: Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore
programme.desc: At 32, Alice Hyatt (Burstyn) watches her dreams slipping away. Instead of a career as a singer, she has an abusive husband, an ill-mannered 12-year-old son and a life in small-town Oklahoma.

programme.title: The Invisible Fight
programme.desc: A young soldier survives an attack from a group of flying kung fu warriors. Hoping to follow in their footsteps, he travels to a local monastery to begin his martial-arts training.

programme.title: The Ideal Palace
programme.desc: Based on the incredible true story of Joseph Ferdinand Cheval comes the remarkable tale of a simple postman who spent 33 years crafting the magnificent 'Ideal Palace'. Everyday Cheval travels along the river Drome from village to village. Quiet and alone, he enjoys the solitude of his rounds, daydreaming about a world full of wonder he can only imagine through postcards. After his wife Philomena gives birth to their daughter Alice, Cheval decides to build Alice a palace fit for a princess. With only his bare hands, his love for his daughter and the dedication of his wife, he starts carefully collecting stones and begins building the historically classified monument.

programme.title: Discovering Film
programme.desc: S13 E2 Denzel Washington Some of the biggest film stars in history rose to fame during the 'golden age' of Hollywood, in the early and mid-20th century. We profile some of these stars who became household names.

programme.title: The Ipcress File
programme.desc: In London, a counter espionage agent deals with his own bureaucracy while investigating the kidnapping and brainwashing of British scientists.

programme.title: All the President's Men
programme.desc: Academy Award winners Robert Redford and Dustin Hoffman star in this true story as Washington Post reporters Carl Bernstein and Bob Woodward, whose investigation of a seemingly minor hotel room break-in uncovers the greatest political scandal in United States history and leads to the downfall of President Richard Nixon.

programme.title: The Invisible Fight
programme.desc: A young soldier survives an attack from a group of flying kung fu warriors. Hoping to follow in their footsteps, he travels to a local monastery to begin his martial-arts training.

programme.title: Man Who Brought Down the White House
programme.desc: The story of FBI special agent Mark Felt, who under the name 'Deep Throat', helped The Washington Post journalists Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein uncover the Watergate scandal in 1972. In the process, Felt risked and ultimately sacrificed everything, including his family and career, to bring what he knew to light.

programme.title: A United Kingdom
programme.desc: The story of Oxford-educated King Seretse Khama of Botswana and how his loving but controversial marriage to white Englishwoman Ruth Williams in 1948 plunged his kingdom into political and diplomatic turmoil.

programme.title: Americanish
programme.desc: Welcome to America: Where dreams come true...ish. Set in Jackson Heights, Queens, New York, career-driven sisters Maryam and Sam Khan, and their fish-out-of-water cousin Ameera navigate romance, culture, career, and family. Americanish highlights different layers of womanhood as they hilariously intersect with cultural and societal expectations.

programme.title: Mad Max: Fury Road
programme.desc: In a post-apocalyptic wasteland, a woman rebels against a tyrannical ruler in search for her homeland with female prisoners, a psychotic worshipper and a drifter named Max.

programme.title: The Informer
programme.desc: Recruited by the FBI, an ex con and former special operations soldier returns to prison to try and take down a Polish drug cartel from the inside.

programme.title: Monster's Ball
programme.desc: A racist prison guard has an affair with a Black woman after her husband, who was sentenced to capital punishment, dies.

programme.title: The Conformist
programme.desc: A member of the secret police in Mussolini's Fascist Italy travels to Paris for his honeymoon, while planning to assassinate his former Professor.

programme.title: A United Kingdom
programme.desc: The story of Oxford-educated King Seretse Khama of Botswana and how his loving but controversial marriage to white Englishwoman Ruth Williams in 1948 plunged his kingdom into political and diplomatic turmoil.

programme.title: Mary Shelley
programme.desc: She will forever be remembered as the writer who gave the world Frankenstein. But the real life story of Mary Shelley - and the creation of her immortal monster - is nearly as fantastical as her fiction.

programme.title: Americanish

Americanish highlights different layers of womanhood as they hilariously intersect with cultural and societal expectations.

programme.title: Blue Jean
programme.desc: In 1988, a closeted teacher is pushed to the brink when a new student threatens to expose her sexuality.

programme.title: Manon Des Sources
programme.desc: The stunning sequel to Jean de Florette. Manon, a beautiful young shepherdess living in the idyllic Provencal countryside, discovers the truth surrounding her father's death and decides to take revenge upon the men responsible.

programme.title: The Ipcress File
programme.desc: In London, a counter espionage agent deals with his own bureaucracy while investigating the kidnapping and brainwashing of British scientists.

programme.title: Hachi: A Dog's Tale
programme.desc: Golden Globe winner Richard Gere stars as Professor Parker Wilson, a distinguished scholar who discovers a lost Akita puppy on his way home from work. Despite initial objections from his wife Hachi endears himself to the Wilson family and grows to be Parker's loyal companion. As their bond grows deeper, a beautiful relationship unfolds, embodying the true spirit of family and loyalty, while inspiring the hearts of an entire town.

programme.title: The Glassworker

Their new home will sit on the wild and windy west coast of King Island, a remote location frequently lashed by the Roaring Forties. King Island isn't known for its eclectic architecture, so the house will stand apart for its unique design in the shape of a whale's tail. Overlooking the sea, it's a house that will truly embrace its location while reflecting the couple's love of the island. This is the journey of Andrew and Dianne establishing their new spiritual home, if it doesn't get blown away.

In the cab crewmates chat about problem hair and emergency toilet breaks. Paramedics V Hodgkins and Rebecca Piddock are called to 61-year-old Richard who's worried he's having a heart attack. Richard has hereditary heart disease and had his first attack four years ago, so he knows the warning signs very well. Meanwhile paramedics Lara Hickman and Stuart Punter are sent to 84-year-old Joyce who's fallen at home. She was found by her carer after being on the floor for several hours. programme.title: Outback Truckers
programme.desc: S3 E12 Episode 12 The outback is one of the world's last wild frontiers. It is vast, untamed, and home to some of the toughest to reach places on Earth. For the giant trucks who roam this epic, harsh country, there's only one way to get from A to B - the hard way. Whether it's taking on scorching deserts, battling torrential rains that turn roads into rivers, or braving a continent's worth of brutal bitumen and desolate dirt, this is a land that can destroy trucks and truckers in a heartbeat. But for the men and women who risk their rigs and their lives to face it, this punishing wilderness is a home away from home. We hit the road train again, for a season of dirt, dramas and dangers, joining some of the toughest, most skilled truckers on the planet, as they haul their massive loads through hell on Earth. Without them, Australia would grind to a halt. Their mission: to get their freight in and their trucks out. In this episode, Sharon has to move a copper mountain, Sludge must shift a freight of highly flammable liquid, and mobile butcher Larry tries to save his meat from the heat.

programme.title: Ice Road Truckers
programme.desc: S10 E6 Bridge To Nowhere For two months out of every year, a group of exceptional men find their way to the Canadian tundra to undertake one of the most dangerous jobs on Earth. In the thick of winter, truckers in giant 18-wheelers carry vital equipment and supplies to miners hundreds of miles away. In blizzard conditions, these truckers travel over ice roads that often take them over frozen lakes. Each man is trained in self survival, from fixing his truck in sub-zero conditions in seconds to escaping from a truck if the ice cracks. On the other end of the journey are miners whose lives depend on the truckers making it to their base, year after year.

programme.title: Outback Truckers
programme.desc: S3 E13 Episode 13 The outback is one of the world's last wild frontiers. It is vast, untamed, and home to some of the toughest to reach places on Earth. For the giant trucks who roam this epic, harsh country, there's only one way to get from A to B - the hard way. Whether it's taking on scorching deserts, battling torrential rains that turn roads into rivers, or braving a continent's worth of brutal bitumen and desolate dirt, this is a land that can destroy trucks and truckers in a heartbeat. But for the men and women who risk their rigs and their lives to face it, this punishing wilderness is a home away from home. We hit the road train again, for a season of dirt, dramas and dangers, joining some of the toughest, most skilled truckers on the planet, as they haul their massive loads through hell on Earth. Without them, Australia would grind to a halt. Their mission: to get their freight in and their trucks out.

programme.title: Food Safari Italy
programme.desc: S1 E5 Episode 5 This episode goes to the far western end of Australia to visit the crayfishermen of the stunning Abrolhos Islands off Geraldton. Maeve spends time with Justin Pirrottina to learn how his father and other Italian fishermen came to fish the area, and tastes how good a 'cray on the barbie' can be. Guy pops in on Melbourne chef Maurizio Esposito to learn the secrets of his delicious crayfish gnocchi recipe. Maeve seeks out the best pizza and visits Melbourne pizzaiolo Alessandro D'Auria of Pizze e Fichi, who has made thousands of pizzas in his years perfecting the art of pizza. Artichokes are loved throughout Italy and were brought to Australia by growers like the Faranda family in Werribee South on the flat plains outside Melbourne. Joe Faranda shows Guy what to look for to get the best, and Guy then makes delicious stuffed artichokes using a recipe passed on to him by his father. Italian gelato has colonised the world's tastebuds, and Sicilian gelato-making brothers Ciccio and Salvatore La Rosa from Gelatomassi in Sydney explain why it's so good.

programme.title: Food Safari Italy
programme.desc: S1 E6 Episode 6 Presenter Guy Grossi meets passionate gardeners Lina and Antonio Siciliano who have created a huge vegetable and herb garden in Melbourne's suburbs that provides them with most of their meals and even the wine to drink with it. Maeve visits her friends the Marino family in Adelaide, who show how they cure prosciutto on a large scale at San Marino Smallgoods. Legendary chef Armando Percuoco from Buon Ricordo restaurant invites Maeve to his country estate and cooks up the simplest dish of pasta with beans, demonstrating how exceptional 'cucina povera' can be. In Melbourne, cheesemaker Giorgio Linguanti takes Guy back to his childhood with the delicious fresh cheeses he makes, including luscious burrata, mozzarella, and ricotta. Loretta Sartori, who once ran her own sweets palace in Melbourne but now spends her time educating troubled youth, cooks a spectacular ricotta cake.

programme.desc: S1 E1 Tuscany And European River Cruise Cameron Daddo and chef Miguel Maestre check into a luxurious 12th century Tuscan castle and indulge in a feast for the senses before hopping aboard a 5-star river cruise along Austria's Danube River. Truffle hunting in a private forest, riding vespas through the Tuscan countryside and an idyllic Italian lunch in an olive grove, Como Castello del Nero is one of Tuscany's best kept secrets. While in Austria, Cam and Miguel board the Riverside Mozart for an ultra-lux cruise along the Danube.

programme.title: Mary Berry at 90: A Lifetime of Cooking
programme.desc: S1 E5 Alan Titchmarsh If Mary has one passion that comes close to cooking, it's her lifelong love of gardening. So it's not surprising that Mary has formed a friendship with one of the country's most respected gardening experts, Alan Titchmarsh. To celebrate her 90th year, Alan has invited Mary for a very special look behind the walls of his magnificent four-acre garden. In these magical surroundings, Mary shows Alan snippets of her old TV shows - how she used to picnic 50 years ago and how she made use of the basic veg of the 1970s. Mary and Alan then make some of her most mouth watering recipes inspired by what we grow: an updated version of a delicious creamy cauliflower soup, Mary's classic smoked salmon, asparagus and dill spaghetti, a salad based around the popular burrata cheese, and teriyaki tuna with ribbon salad. Finally, it's Alan's chance to make a cake for the first time - Mary's classic apple cake served with cream.

programme.desc: S1 E1 The Night Stalker - Delroy Grant Part 1 Former Detective Chief Inspector Colin Sutton spent 30 years in the police force, a career that saw him lead many of the highest profile and successful murder investigations of his generation, and although he'll forever be associated with the arrest and conviction of serial killer Levi Bellfield and 'Night Stalker' Delroy Grant, his career was so much more. In this series, Sutton revisits cases he led and explores everything from the crime itself through to the breakthrough moment when the suspect was identified and arrested. It's a mix of red-blooded gumption, unbridled greed, and a love of nature that make Anchoragites one of America's most unique breed of citizens. And in 1996, it was also home to fisherman Kent Leppink and his soon-to-be bride, Mechele Hughes. But before they could tie the knot, Kent was found murdered in the wilderness outside of town. Even though Mechele's alleged greed - complete with a million-dollar life insurance policy just months before Kent's death - seemed to be a motive for murder, the investigation turned cold. That is, until 2004, when an unexpected confession revealed a love rectangle of sinister proportions.

programme.title: Forensic Files
programme.desc: S4 E3 Ultimate Betrayal Debora Green lost two children in a fire that burnt down her mansion late one night. Routine procedures occurred and both Debora Green and her previous husband Mike Farrar were questioned. Suspicions arose when Debora refused to cooperate during questioning. Police then questioned Mike and uncovered disturbing stories proving Debora was dangerous. She had poisoned Mike during their separation and told him he would only get custody of the children over their dead bodies. Debora's singed hair and the initial location of the fire proved her involvement in the arson.

programme.title: Forensic Files
programme.desc: S4 E4 Cement The Case Shirley Andronowich's body was found one morning after being brutally murdered and mutilated. Witnesses told police Shirley and her husband Ed were seen fighting in a bar the night before. Police first suspected Ed and even arrested him after confessing to the murder. However, all forensic evidence proved that Ed had actually nothing to do with the murder. Police received a call around a year later about a Mark Jarman who talked about being connected to Shirley's murder. Once investigated, police found that his identity matched all the evidence found at the crime scene. Jarman stated there was no motive for the murder.

programme.title: Forensic Files
programme.desc: S4 E5 Innocence Lost Five-year-old Melissa Brannen disappeared from a Christmas party in 1989. The fibres on her clothes were the only means for police to determine her abductor. Police grew suspicious of Cal Hughes who was washing his clothes at 1am when they came to his home. They searched his car and found several fibres similar to the clothes Melissa had worn to the party. However, there was no way to test the fibres until an investigator's wife remembered seeing Melissa's outfit in a catalogue. The same outfit was taken from another customer and tested. The fibres matched and Cal Hughes was convicted of abduction with intent to harm.

programme.title: Forensic Files
programme.desc: S4 E6 Til Death Do Us Part Robert Curley was diagnosed with Guillain-Barre syndrome when he first came to the hospital with excruciating leg pains. Doctors became suspicious, however, during Robert's second admission and tested him for thallium poisoning, which proved positive. Robert died shortly after. A second autopsy proved that Robert ingested more poison a few days before his death. Investigators also discovered that Joann was waiting to collect her previous husband's life insurance due to his accidental death and disagreed with the way Robert wanted to spend it. Joann would then collect additional life insurance if Robert suffered from an accidental death. Joann was convicted of Robert's murder six years later.

programme.title: Outback Truckers
programme.desc: S3 E12 Episode 12 The outback is one of the world's last wild frontiers. It is vast, untamed, and home to some of the toughest to reach places on Earth. For the giant trucks who roam this epic, harsh country, there's only one way to get from A to B - the hard way. Whether it's taking on scorching deserts, battling torrential rains that turn roads into rivers, or braving a continent's worth of brutal bitumen and desolate dirt, this is a land that can destroy trucks and truckers in a heartbeat. But for the men and women who risk their rigs and their lives to face it, this punishing wilderness is a home away from home. We hit the road train again, for a season of dirt, dramas and dangers, joining some of the toughest, most skilled truckers on the planet, as they haul their massive loads through hell on Earth. Without them, Australia would grind to a halt. Their mission: to get their freight in and their trucks out. In this episode, Sharon has to move a copper mountain, Sludge must shift a freight of highly flammable liquid, and mobile butcher Larry tries to save his meat from the heat.

programme.title: Ice Road Truckers
programme.desc: S10 E6 Bridge To Nowhere For two months out of every year, a group of exceptional men find their way to the Canadian tundra to undertake one of the most dangerous jobs on Earth. In the thick of winter, truckers in giant 18-wheelers carry vital equipment and supplies to miners hundreds of miles away. In blizzard conditions, these truckers travel over ice roads that often take them over frozen lakes. Each man is trained in self survival, from fixing his truck in sub-zero conditions in seconds to escaping from a truck if the ice cracks. On the other end of the journey are miners whose lives depend on the truckers making it to their base, year after year.

programme.title: Ice Road Truckers
programme.desc: S9 E10 Icy Alliance For two months out of every year, a group of exceptional men find their way to the Canadian tundra to undertake one of the most dangerous jobs on earth. In the thick of winter, truckers in giant eighteen wheelers carry vital equipment and supplies to miners hundreds of miles away. In blizzard conditions, these truckers travel over ice roads that often take them over frozen lakes. Each man is trained in self survival, from fixing his truck in sub zero conditions in seconds to escaping from a truck if the ice cracks. On the other end of the journey are miners whose lives depend on the truckers making it to their base, year after year. The episodes will form a narrative arch - taking the viewer on a journey from when the experienced and novice truckers first sign up for the season, to the last truck making it back to base.

programme.title: Outback Truckers
programme.desc: S3 E13 Episode 13 The outback is one of the world's last wild frontiers. It is vast, untamed, and home to some of the toughest to reach places on Earth. For the giant trucks who roam this epic, harsh country, there's only one way to get from A to B - the hard way. Whether it's taking on scorching deserts, battling torrential rains that turn roads into rivers, or braving a continent's worth of brutal bitumen and desolate dirt, this is a land that can destroy trucks and truckers in a heartbeat. But for the men and women who risk their rigs and their lives to face it, this punishing wilderness is a home away from home. We hit the road train again, for a season of dirt, dramas and dangers, joining some of the toughest, most skilled truckers on the planet, as they haul their massive loads through hell on Earth. Without them, Australia would grind to a halt. Their mission: to get their freight in and their trucks out.

programme.title: Food Safari Italy
programme.desc: S1 E5 Episode 5 This episode goes to the far western end of Australia to visit the crayfishermen of the stunning Abrolhos Islands off Geraldton. Maeve spends time with Justin Pirrottina to learn how his father and other Italian fishermen came to fish the area, and tastes how good a 'cray on the barbie' can be. Guy pops in on Melbourne chef Maurizio Esposito to learn the secrets of his delicious crayfish gnocchi recipe. Maeve seeks out the best pizza and visits Melbourne pizzaiolo Alessandro D'Auria of Pizze e Fichi, who has made thousands of pizzas in his years perfecting the art of pizza. Artichokes are loved throughout Italy and were brought to Australia by growers like the Faranda family in Werribee South on the flat plains outside Melbourne. Joe Faranda shows Guy what to look for to get the best, and Guy then makes delicious stuffed artichokes using a recipe passed on to him by his father. Italian gelato has colonised the world's tastebuds, and Sicilian gelato-making brothers Ciccio and Salvatore La Rosa from Gelatomassi in Sydney explain why it's so good.

programme.title: Food Safari Italy
programme.desc: S1 E6 Episode 6 Presenter Guy Grossi meets passionate gardeners Lina and Antonio Siciliano who have created a huge vegetable and herb garden in Melbourne's suburbs that provides them with most of their meals and even the wine to drink with it. Maeve visits her friends the Marino family in Adelaide, who show how they cure prosciutto on a large scale at San Marino Smallgoods. Legendary chef Armando Percuoco from Buon Ricordo restaurant invites Maeve to his country estate and cooks up the simplest dish of pasta with beans, demonstrating how exceptional 'cucina povera' can be. In Melbourne, cheesemaker Giorgio Linguanti takes Guy back to his childhood with the delicious fresh cheeses he makes, including luscious burrata, mozzarella, and ricotta. Loretta Sartori, who once ran her own sweets palace in Melbourne but now spends her time educating troubled youth, cooks a spectacular ricotta cake.

programme.desc: S1 E1 Tuscany And European River Cruise Cameron Daddo and chef Miguel Maestre check into a luxurious 12th century Tuscan castle and indulge in a feast for the senses before hopping aboard a 5-star river cruise along Austria's Danube River. Truffle hunting in a private forest, riding vespas through the Tuscan countryside and an idyllic Italian lunch in an olive grove, Como Castello del Nero is one of Tuscany's best kept secrets. While in Austria, Cam and Miguel board the Riverside Mozart for an ultra-lux cruise along the Danube.

programme.title: Mary Berry at 90: A Lifetime of Cooking
programme.desc: S1 E5 Alan Titchmarsh If Mary has one passion that comes close to cooking, it's her lifelong love of gardening. So it's not surprising that Mary has formed a friendship with one of the country's most respected gardening experts, Alan Titchmarsh. To celebrate her 90th year, Alan has invited Mary for a very special look behind the walls of his magnificent four-acre garden. In these magical surroundings, Mary shows Alan snippets of her old TV shows - how she used to picnic 50 years ago and how she made use of the basic veg of the 1970s. Mary and Alan then make some of her most mouth watering recipes inspired by what we grow: an updated version of a delicious creamy cauliflower soup, Mary's classic smoked salmon, asparagus and dill spaghetti, a salad based around the popular burrata cheese, and teriyaki tuna with ribbon salad. Finally, it's Alan's chance to make a cake for the first time - Mary's classic apple cake served with cream.
